newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL INTERBANK RATES FALL SLIGHTLY ON BILL MATURITY.
newsitem.headline: KL INTERBANK RATES FALL SLIGHTLY ON BILL MATURITY.

text.p: Malaysian interbank rates fell slightly on Friday morning after the maturity of a one-billion ringgit Bank Negara bill issue, dealers said.
The one-week interbank rate was down at 7.0 percent against 7.5 percent on Thursday.
One-month money stood at 7.8/9 percent against 7.8/8.0 percent, while three-month was at 7.85/95 percent against 7.9/8.0 percent.
Friday's maturity of Bank Negara bills has not been rolled over.

"Rates are down mainly because of the maturity," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "The market is still quite tight and rates are unlikely to fall much from current levels unless there is a big inflow."
Dealers noted continued lending by foreign banks long on ringgit.
"Foreign banks are lending one-month money at 7.75 percent this morning. They are still long on ringgit," said another dealer.
The overnight rate was expected to trade between 5.8 and 6.5 percent, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were steady to reflect softer interbank rates.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was unchanged at 92.43, or an implied yield of 7.57 percent.
The December contract was also steady at 92.64, or 7.36 percent.
